---------------------------------------------------------------------------
FISCAL_INSTITUTIONS -- taxes, rent, mortgages, tithes, stipends, wages, and collection (Phase 011)
---------------------------------------------------------------------------
One entry per institution, extracted from the eight seeds named in each entry's `seeds`. An entry says
who levies and who pays, the base and rate (and who sets the rate), the schedule, which purse the coin
moves into or out of (world/fiscal.json FISCAL_PURSES), who must physically be present to collect or
hand over the coin (`agent_role`, `requires_colocation`), what a missed payment does (`on_missed`), and the
rule names it came from (`seed_rules`). Each seed rule name appears exactly once in these entries or in
FISCAL_BACKEND_OWNED. Seed files stay untouched; bigville/seeds/gen_fiscal_<name>.json is generated from
this table by tools/generate_seeds.py.

WHAT THE WORLD DOES: records each due obligation (an Obligation node with its amount, base, and rate),
moves coin on a payment or collection when the coin is there and the parties stand on the same cell,
and records arrears when a payer short of coin is at the payee's cell. Nothing else happens on a miss:
no eviction, no foreclosure, no service stops by itself.

WHAT THE BACKEND DOES: sets rates and amounts (assess_obligation), decides whether to pay, collect, or
skip a payment, collects with a hired collector, decides on eviction, foreclosure, graft, and levies. These
choices are in FISCAL_BACKEND_OWNED with their reasons.

Rates and amounts are not in this pack: a seed's numbers (council base_rate_bp, tithe_bp, rent, salary) are
agent-set values, so `rate.value` is null. The rounding the seeds use is round_bp in domains/world_affordances.py,
IDiv(amount*bp+5000, 10000) on whole coins.

Public spread in `knowledge.public` is authored judgement (APPROX), read by domains/knowledge.py.
Office conditions in `understanding_requires` name an office's authority (records, executive, deliberative), not the office, so a pack that renames offices keeps valid specs (as Phase 019).

council_tax.title: council tax on the taxable base
council_tax.payers: residents with a taxable base (the `taxable` attribute)
council_tax.payees: the treasury purse, received by the clerk-treasurer
council_tax.schedule: when the payer chooses to pay, face to face with the clerk (no automatic debit)
council_tax.records: the treasury ledger: purse.recorded moves with every payment; purse discrepancy = coin - recorded

treasury_salaries.title: salaries paid from the treasury
treasury_salaries.payers: the treasury purse, paid out by the clerk-treasurer
treasury_salaries.schedule: each period, when the clerk pays out

on_missed.note: a short purse leaves the salary unpaid and recorded as arrears; the treasury is depleted when its coin is 0 after taxes have come in

treasury_salaries.records: the treasury ledger (a salary is a recorded outflow)

rent_and_tenancy.title: rent paid by a tenant to a landlord
rent_and_tenancy.payees: the landlord, or a hired collector acting for the landlord
rent_and_tenancy.schedule: each period, handed to the landlord or to the hired collector

on_missed.note: a missed rent is recorded as arrears on the obligation and nothing else changes; eviction is the landlord's choice (FISCAL_BACKEND_OWNED bf_evict)

rent_and_tenancy.records: the obligation: amount, paid, periods_paid, arrears

mortgage.title: mortgage repaid to a lender
mortgage.payers: the homeowner who holds the mortgage
mortgage.payees: the lender (no bank exists in the world yet; bigville_fin_bank is out of scope)

base.note: the balance the interest rate applies to; the backend adds the principal part to the amount it assesses

mortgage.schedule: each period, handed to the lender

on_missed.note: a missed payment is recorded as arrears; the seed's balance accrual on a miss is a lender's term applied by the backend, and foreclosure is the lender's choice (bf_foreclose)

mortgage.records: the obligation: amount, paid, periods_paid, arrears

tithe_and_donation.title: tithe to the church, a committed share of income
tithe_and_donation.payers: a resident who has committed to tithe
tithe_and_donation.payees: the church funds purse, received by the pastor
tithe_and_donation.schedule: each period the giver chooses to pay
tithe_and_donation.records: the church funds ledger and the obligation

church_stipend_and_charity.title: the pastor's stipend and charity to the poor, paid from church funds
church_stipend_and_charity.payers: the church funds purse, paid out by the pastor
church_stipend_and_charity.payees: the pastor (stipend), and residents the church helps (charity)
church_stipend_and_charity.schedule: each period, when the pastor pays out

on_missed.note: a short church purse leaves the stipend or a charity payment unpaid and recorded as arrears; the church is defunct when its funds are 0 after donations have come in; losing the tied parsonage is the church's choice (FISCAL_BACKEND_OWNED fc_parsonage_precarious)

church_stipend_and_charity.records: the church funds ledger (stipend and charity are recorded outflows)

wages.title: wages paid by an employer to a worker
wages.payees: the worker, such as a hired collector
wages.records: the obligation: amount, paid, periods_paid, arrears

hired_collection.title: rent collected by a hired collector who delivers it to the landlord
hired_collection.payees: the landlord, through the hired collector
hired_collection.schedule: when the hired collector reaches the tenant
hired_collection.collector: the hired collector named on the obligation
hired_collection.records: the obligation: held (collected, not yet delivered), delivered, and skimmed (held but not delivered)

school_fund.title: the schoolmaster's pay, which decides whether the school is open

on_missed.note: the school is open when the schoolmaster was paid and closed when he was not; the world does not publish that state yet

FISCAL_BACKEND_OWNED.reason: the council decides the rate; the world records an assessment (assess_obligation) and never sets one
graft is a choice to take treasury coin without an obligation; the world has no purse withdrawal (Phase 041)
one resident levying coin from another is a social choice, not an institution in the data
foreclosure is the lender's choice; the world records arrears and does not take the house
eviction is the landlord's choice; the world records arrears and does not remove the tenant
distress is a resident's affect, which belongs to cognition
an owner's equity is a valuation the resident holds; the pack has no appraisal
a mortgagor's equity is a valuation the resident holds; the pack has no appraisal
a change in house value is a market judgement, not a physical fact
a landlord's choice to raise rent (a rate setting) and the coercion it carries
the seed's job wage (revenue less crowding) is a market figure residents read; no world wage is paid from it
a resident chooses to change work, given the wage gap and role identity
production by workers is part of the economic loop, not an institution; the physical stock is in the pack's CROPS and RESOURCE_DEPOSITS
a price falling on a glut is an outcome of sellers and buyers; the world has no price-setting rule
a price rising on scarcity is an outcome of sellers and buyers; the world has no price-setting rule
the derived market wage is information for residents; the wage they pay is their own choice
a resident chooses to move to a better-paid trade
giving when flush is a resident's choice; the transfer itself is an ordinary pay_obligation to church_funds
ending the tie to the parsonage is the church's choice; the world has no tied-housing record
co-regulation changes a resident's affect, which belongs to cognition
